sections.heading: 2. Description of Service

The Service supports both the 2014 and 2024 rulesets and is provided for personal, non-commercial tabletop preparation use.

sections.heading: 4. Your Content

You retain all rights to your User Content. By using the Service you confirm that your User Content does not infringe on the rights of any third party.

Encounter difficulty, XP budgets, and scaled statistics are computational aids and should always be reviewed by the Dungeon Master before use at the table.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.description: Important information about the nature and limitations of CRealizr.

sections.heading: Fan-Made, Unofficial Content
body: CRealizr is a fan-made toolkit created by and for Dungeons & Dragons players and Dungeon Masters. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, sponsored by, or associated with Wizards of the Coast in any way. "Dungeons & Dragons", "D&D", and all related logos and trademarks are the property of Wizards of the Coast LLC.
Rules and reference content used by the tools are drawn from the System Reference Document (SRD), made available under the applicable Open Gaming License / Creative Commons license.

sections.heading: No Artificial Intelligence
body: CRealizr does not use artificial intelligence, machine learning, or generative AI models anywhere in its tools. Every encounter suggestion, monster scaling calculation, travel encounter, and item blueprint is produced by deterministic, rule-based logic written and reviewed by human developers — the same kind of math a DM would do by hand, just faster.

For the development process of the website, AI is only being used to implement testing scenarios, scaffold & organize code and handle website versioning, in order to deliver features in a faster, yet effective manner. No process or item in the toolkit is ever processed by AI, nor any user data is processed without user consent from Google Analytics.
None of the data you enter is sent to an AI service or third-party model. The toolkit is, and will remain, 100% human-made.

sections.heading: Not Professional or Rules-Authoritative Advice
body: Encounter difficulty ratings, experience point budgets, monster scaling, and item generation are computational estimates intended to speed up game preparation. They are not a substitute for the official rulebooks or the Dungeon Master's own judgment, and should be adjusted as needed for your table.

sections.heading: Accuracy of Content
body: While we strive for accuracy across both the 2014 and 2024 rulesets, CRealizr is provided without any guarantee that outputs are complete, error-free, or perfectly balanced for every table. Use generated content at your own discretion.

sections.heading: Local Data Storage
body: Custom monsters and similar user-created data are stored only in your browser's local storage. We do not host, back up, or have access to this data. Clearing your browser data, using a different browser, or switching devices will remove it — export your library regularly to keep a backup.

sections.heading: External Links
body: The Service may link to third-party sites, such as GitHub. We are not responsible for the content, accuracy, or practices of any linked external site.

sections.heading: No Warranty & Limitation of Liability
body: CRealizr is provided free of charge, "as is", without warranty of any kind. To the fullest extent permitted by law, the CRealizr team disclaims liability for any damages or losses arising from use of the Service.

sections.heading: Contact

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: What personal data CRealizr processes, why, and your rights under GDPR.

sections.heading: 1. Who We Are
body: CRealizr is an independent, fan-made D&D toolkit. For the purposes of data protection law, the CRealizr team acts as the data controller for any personal data processed through this site. You can reach us at contact@crealizr.net for any privacy question or request.

sections.heading: 2. What We Collect
body: Contact form: when you use the contact form, we process the name, email address, and message you submit, solely to respond to your inquiry.

Automatically, for abuse prevention: when you submit the contact form, our server briefly reads your IP address and browser user-agent string to rate-limit repeated submissions and (if enabled) verify a Cloudflare Turnstile CAPTCHA challenge. This information is kept only in server memory for up to 10 minutes, is never written to a database or disk, and is lost whenever the server restarts.

Only if you accept our cookie banner: we load Google Tag Manager, which may collect analytics data (such as pages visited and general usage patterns) via cookies. This never loads before you accept, and you can decline or withdraw consent at any time. See Section 7 (Cookies) below for details.
Beyond the above, we do not use tracking pixels or advertising scripts anywhere on this site, and we do not sell or build advertising profiles of visitors.

sections.heading: 3. Legal Basis for Processing
body: We process contact form submissions based on your consent, given by voluntarily submitting the form (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR), and on our legitimate interest in responding to inquiries and keeping the form free of spam and abuse (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

sections.heading: 4. Who We Share Data With
body: Email delivery: your contact form submission is sent via an SMTP email provider to our inbox. That message is then subject to that provider's and our own mailbox's normal retention practices — we do not separately store a copy in a database.

Cloudflare Turnstile: when CAPTCHA verification is enabled, your IP address and the CAPTCHA token are sent to Cloudflare to confirm you are not a bot. Cloudflare acts as an independent processor for this check; see Cloudflare's Privacy Policy for details.
Google Tag Manager: only if you accept our cookie banner, usage data is shared with Google as described in Google's Privacy Policy. Declining or withdrawing consent stops this sharing going forward.
We do not sell personal data, and we do not share it with any other third party.

sections.heading: 5. International Transfers
body: Cloudflare and Google both operate global networks, which may process the data described above outside your country of residence, including outside the European Economic Area. Both providers offer Standard Contractual Clauses and other safeguards for such transfers.

sections.heading: 6. Data Retention
body: Rate-limiting data (IP address, user-agent) is held in server memory for at most 10 minutes and is never persisted. Contact form emails remain in our inbox for as long as reasonably needed to handle your inquiry, unless you ask us to delete them sooner.

sections.heading: 7. Cookies
body: By default, CRealizr sets no cookies at all — no analytics cookies, no advertising cookies, and no session cookies. The language you browse in is stored in the page URL (e.g. /en/, /de/), not in a cookie.

If you click "Accept" on our cookie banner, we load Google Tag Manager, which may set analytics cookies (such as Google Analytics) to help us understand how visitors use CRealizr. Nothing is loaded until you accept, and you can withdraw your consent at any time via "Cookie Preferences" in the footer, which stops future cookies but does not automatically delete ones already set by your browser — clear them via your browser's settings if needed.

sections.heading: 8. Local Storage on Your Device
body: Your theme, saved battle-map layouts, any homebrew monsters you create in My Bestiary, and a few small UI preferences (like whether you've dismissed the "rotate your device" tip) are stored only in your own browser's local storage or IndexedDB. None of it ever reaches our servers or is visible to us — clear your browser data at any time to remove it.

sections.heading: 9. Your Rights Under GDPR
body: If you are in the European Economic Area (or a jurisdiction with equivalent protections), you have the right to access, correct, or delete your personal data, restrict or object to its processing, request a copy in a portable format, and withdraw consent at any time. To exercise any of these rights, contact us at contact@crealizr.net. You also have the right to lodge a complaint with your local data protection supervisory authority.

sections.heading: 10. Children's Privacy
body: CRealizr is not directed at children under 16, and we do not knowingly collect personal data from them. If you believe a child has submitted personal data to us, please contact us and we will delete it.

sections.heading: 11. Changes to This Policy
body: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Continued use of the Service after changes are posted constitutes acceptance of the revised policy.

sections.heading: 12. Contact
body: Questions about this Privacy Policy or your data can be sent to contact@crealizr.net.

encounterBuilderDocs.title: Encounter Builder – How It Works
encounterBuilderDocs.description: Complete reference for every feature in the Encounter Builder — party setup, two calculation modes, the interactive battlefield, and cover mechanics.

sections.heading: Inputs
sections.html:
• Party size — number of characters (1–8). Quick-preset chips for 3/4/5/6.
  • Average level — 1–20. Drives both XP thresholds and CR target calculations.
  • Difficulty — easy, medium, hard, or deadly.
  • Ruleset — 2014 DMG or 2024 Player's Handbook tables.
  • Formation — Solo Boss (one dominant enemy, optionally with minions) or Horde/Group (mixed-CR mob).

sections.heading: Calculation Mode
sections.html:
The Calculation Mode toggle switches between two distinct approaches. Both produce the same suggestion card format; what changes is the math behind them.

XP Budget mode (default)

Full D&D 5e encounter-budget flow:

  1. Look up the per-character XP threshold for the chosen level and difficulty.
  2. Multiply by party size: budget = threshold[level][difficulty] × partySize.
  3. For each candidate group of monsters, compute: adjustedXP = Σ(count × xpEach) × encounterMultiplier(totalCount).
  4. Keep suggestions where fit = min(budget, adjustedXP) / max(budget, adjustedXP) ≥ 0.7.
  5. Sort by highest fit, then lower adjustedXP. Return top 12.

The Budget Type sub-toggle switches between Encounter budget (single session) and Daily budget (≈3.4× encounter budget, for full adventuring days).

Encounter multipliers

  • 1 monster → ×1
  • 2 → ×1.5
  • 3–6 → ×2
  • 7–10 → ×2.5
  • 11–14 → ×3
  • 15+ → ×4

CR Match mode

No XP math. Suggestions are generated purely by comparing challenge ratings to the party level:

  1. Compute a target CR per difficulty offset: easy: level−2 · medium: level · hard: level+1 · deadly: level+3 (min 1/8).
  2. Scale by party size: crBudget = targetCR × (partySize / 4).
  3. For each candidate group, compute a CR encounter weight: crWeight = Σ(cr × count) × √encounterMultiplier(totalCount).
  4. Keep suggestions where fit = min(crBudget, crWeight) / max(crBudget, crWeight) ≥ 0.5.

The Max Beatable CR displayed in the party card is crTarget × (partySize / 4), formatted as a challenge rating — the single-monster ceiling the party can handle at the selected difficulty.

No accuracy labels (On Target / Over Budget) are shown in CR Match mode because the CR tables already define an unambiguous answer; percentage fit is redundant.

sections.heading: Solo Boss vs Horde/Group
sections.html:
Solo Boss

Enumerates boss CRs near the target, optionally pairing them with lower-CR minions. With Include Minions on, the tool searches for related monsters (by terrain, affiliation, or genus via the Relation Filter) to populate the minion slot.

Horde / Group

Builds mixed-CR compositions. The Mix Types setting (2–5) caps how many distinct CR types appear in one suggestion. For N total monsters and T types:

  • Enumerate all CR combinations of size T.
  • Enumerate all ways to split N into T positive integer counts.
  • Keep combinations whose budget fit meets the threshold.

sections.heading: Relation Filter
sections.html:
Available when minions are enabled (Solo) or always in Group mode. Restricts candidates to monsters that share a chosen property with a benchmark creature at the target CR:

  • Any Species — no filter.
  • Same Terrain — monsters whose terrain list overlaps.
  • Same Affiliation — monsters with the same faction tag.
  • Same Genus — monsters of the same creature genus (e.g. undead, dragon).

sections.heading: Battlefield Map
sections.html:
An interactive flat-top hex grid. Party members (green) and enemies (gold/red for bosses) are placed automatically when a suggestion is selected. All nodes are draggable.

Toolbar modes

  • W — Move: drag nodes freely. Multi-select with Ctrl/Cmd/Shift+click to drag several nodes at once.
  • A — Env Hazard: click an empty hex to place an environment hazard (orange).
  • S — Spell Hazard: click an empty hex to place a spell hazard (purple).
  • C — Cover: click an empty hex to place a cover obstacle (bright blue).
  • L — Lock Camera: freezes panning while you drag nodes.
  • + / − — zoom in / out.
  • Esc — return to Move mode and unlock camera.

Removing nodes

Each node shows a small × button. Removing a party node decrements the outer party size counter. Removing an enemy node persists across re-syncs from the same suggestion and resets only when a new suggestion is selected.

Grid

The grid is infinite in all directions. Pan by dragging the background. Pinch-to-zoom works on touch devices. The view auto-centers on the current encounter nodes whenever the suggestion or party size changes.

Mobile fullscreen

On mobile, the battlefield only opens as a fullscreen overlay with a touch-friendly bottom toolbar — tap Open Battlefield to enter, and ← Exit to return.

sections.heading: Hazards & Area of Effect
sections.html:
Both hazard types (environment and spell) support an AoE — a Sphere/Cube/Cylinder burst by default, or a Cone/Line for spell hazards, in any of the 6 hex directions (0–3 hexes, default 1). After placing a hazard, open its editor to adjust the shape, direction, and radius.

  • The AoE fills covered hexes with a matching tint (orange = env, purple = spell).
  • Any Cover node within the AoE turns the hex blue — the cover blocks the hazard there.
  • Party or enemy nodes inside an unprotected AoE hex glow with the hazard's colour.
  • Hazards stack on top of any other node. Cover, party, and enemy nodes remain exclusive (one per hex).

sections.heading: Cover
sections.html:
Cover follows standard D&D 5e rules. Three levels are available via the node editor:

  • Half Cover — +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws.
  • Three-Quarters Cover — +5 bonus to AC and Dexterity saving throws.
  • Full Cover — cannot be targeted directly by attacks or spells.

The Advantages / Disadvantages section in the Party card automatically lists every party member who is adjacent (1 hex away) to a cover node, showing the best cover level available.

sections.heading: Node Editor
sections.html:
Click any node to open its editor. Available fields vary by node type:

  • All nodes — custom label.
  • Hazards — notes text, AoE shape/direction (spell only), and radius (0 = single hex, 1–3 = expanding rings).
  • Cover — cover level (Half / Three-Quarters / Full).

encounterBuilderDocs.note: Rules basis: D&D 5e 2014 DMG encounter building guidelines and PHB cover rules. Use as a starting point and adjust to your table.

monsterScalerDocs.title: Monster Scaler – How It Works
monsterScalerDocs.description: Documents the exact steps and formulas used by the Monster Scaler. The CR matrix is identical across the 2014 and 2024 rulesets, so scaling works the same regardless of which sourcebook a monster comes from.

sections.heading: Inputs
sections.html:
• Source monster stat block: name, size/type, current CR, and stats (AC, HP, STR/DEX/CON/INT/WIS/CHA).
  • Optional action list used to estimate DPR from damage expressions (e.g. 1d6+2).
  • Target CR (supports fractional CRs 1/8, 1/4, 1/2 and CR 1–30).
  • AC source: Dex-based, equipped armor, or natural armor — plus an optional shield toggle.
  • Optional per-ability-score bonuses.

sections.heading: CR row lookup
sections.html: We look up two rows from the CR matrix: one for the source CR and one for the target CR. Each row contains reference values for proficiency bonus, expected AC, HP, attack bonus, DPR, and save DC — the highest row with row.cr ≤ cr is used.

sections.heading: Damage Per Round (DPR) estimation
sections.html:
If the monster has actions with damage strings, we estimate average damage for each action and sum:

  • For each token like XdY (e.g. 2d6), expected value = X × (Y + 1) / 2.
  • An optional flat modifier ±N is added once to that action's total.
  • Non-dice numbers are parsed as a flat value where possible.

The per-action averages are summed and rounded to the nearest integer. If no actions are provided, the scaler skips the DPR ratio and shows the target CR's expected DPR as an absolute reference instead.

sections.heading: HP scaling
sections.html:
HP is scaled proportionally, preserving how far above or below the CR baseline the original monster sits:

hpScale = tgtRow.hp / max(1, srcRow.hp)

finalHP = round(srcHP × hpScale), with a minimum of 1.

Example: a CR 1 monster with 156 HP (2× the CR 1 baseline of 78) scaled to CR 5 (baseline 138) yields round(156 × 138/78) = 276 — still roughly 2× the CR 5 baseline.

sections.heading: AC scaling
sections.html:
AC is derived independently of the CR matrix, from one of three sources you choose, plus an optional shield:

  • Dex-based: 10 + Dex modifier — for unarmored creatures relying on agility.
  • Equipped armor: 10 + armor bonus — the bonus you enter for whatever armor the creature wears.
  • Natural armor: a flat value you enter directly (e.g. a dragon's or tortle's natural armor) — not added to 10.

A held shield always adds a flat +2 on top of any of the three sources.

Dex-based and natural armor are inherent to the creature and are capped at AC 30 for monsters — mirroring how player AC caps at 20 from Dex/natural sources alone. Equipped armor and a shield are treated as items and are allowed to push AC past the cap: finalAC = (armor ? 10 + armorBonus : clamp(inherentAC, 1, 30)) + (shield ? 2 : 0). The Tarrasque's AC of 25 is a good reference point for how high natural armor can go without ever needing an item.

Situational cover (see the Encounter Builder's cover mechanic) can further raise effective AC during combat, but isn't part of the monster's base stat block.

sections.heading: Ability score scaling (STR/DEX/CON/INT/WIS/CHA)
sections.html:
We scale ability scores by modifier steps, not by raw points:

  1. Compute CR difference: crDiff = targetCR − sourceCR.
  2. Increase the ability modifier by floor(crDiff / 2) steps. Example: from CR 1 to CR 5, crDiff=4 ⇒ +2 modifier steps.
  3. Map the new modifier back to the nearest canonical score using the standard "score ⇒ modifier" table.
  4. Apply any per-ability bonus, then clamp to the 1–30 range.

sections.heading: Attack bonus advice
sections.html:
• Best attack ability modifier: atkAbilityMod = max(mod(STR), mod(DEX)) for scaled stats.
  • Matrix baseline change: attackDelta = tgtRow.atkb − srcRow.atkb.
  • Adjust for the monster's own stat change: atkAbilityMod − srcAtkMod.
  • Suggested: finalAttackBonus = round(srcRow.atkb + attackDelta + atkAbilityMod − srcAtkMod).

sections.heading: Save DC advice
sections.html:
Suggested save DC starts from the target row's DC and shifts with the monster's INT modifier change (as a spellcasting-style proxy):

finalSaveDC = tgtRow.save_dc + (mod(INT_scaled) − mod(INT_source))

sections.heading: DPR reference
sections.html:
When actions are provided, the scaler reports a scale factor to help you retune damage:

  • srcDPR: estimated from input actions.
  • tgtDPR: midpoint of the official DMG damage/round range for the target CR, used only for the ratio.
  • dprScale = tgtDPR / max(1, srcDPR) — multiply each action's damage by this to hit the target band.

The monster's displayed dpr field is always the official DMG range itself (e.g. 33–38 at CR 5) — not a synthetic band computed around a single number.

sections.heading: Bounds, clamps & determinism
sections.html:
• AC is clamped to 5–30 after all adjustments.
  • Ability scores are clamped to 1–30.
  • HP has a minimum of 1.

The scaler is fully deterministic. All matrix values are the midpoint of the official DMG ranges. No randomness is applied at runtime — same inputs always produce the same output.

sections.heading: CR Matrix Reference
sections.html: These are the exact baseline values used by the scaler, taken directly from the live data layer. The table is the official DMG "Monster Statistics by Challenge Rating" table and is identical for the 2014 and 2024 rulesets — CRealizr uses a single unified matrix regardless of which sourcebook a monster is drawn from.

monsterScalerDocs.note: HP and Damage/Round values are the official DMG CR table ranges — HP is shown as its midpoint, DPR is shown as the full range. Attack bonuses and Save DCs match the official table exactly.

artifactForgeDocs.title: Artifact Forge – How It Works
artifactForgeDocs.description: Details on rarity by level, suggested bonuses, and the item blueprint produced by the Artifact Forge.

sections.heading: Inputs
sections.html:
• Item name (optional)
  • Item type: Weapon | Armor | Wand | Wondrous
  • Player level (1–20) used for tuning
  • Player Attunement Requirement setup
  • Optional target monster tags to annotate effectiveness
  • Optional crafting ingredients with quantity (and optional unit)
  • Optional crafting cost, time, and special requirement (place, profession, or specialist)
  • Optional lore description (up to 100 words)

sections.heading: Quick actions
sections.html:
• Use Example to prefill a complete artifact blueprint.
  • Lock Mechanics to keep type/level/attunement while refining flavor.
  • Clear Flavor or Clear Crafting to iterate quickly.

sections.heading: Mechanics vs Flavor
sections.html: The forge separates mechanical output (rarity, bonuses, tuned level) from flavor (ingredients, requirements, and lore). This keeps balance adjustments fast while you iterate on story.

sections.heading: Export preview
sections.html: The preview panel mirrors the JSON output so you can copy or screenshot it quickly.

sections.heading: Rarity by level
sections.html:
Rarity is assigned from player level via a simple curve:

  • ≤3 → Common
  • 4–6 → Uncommon
  • 7–10 → Rare
  • 11–16 → Very Rare
  • 17–20 → Legendary

sections.heading: Suggested bonuses
sections.html:
Bonuses are intentionally conservative and keyed to rarity bands:

  • Magic bonus: Common 0, Uncommon +1, Rare +2, Very Rare +3, Legendary +3
  • Avg damage bonus: mirrors magic bonus by rarity
  • Save DC (for wands): Common/Uncommon 13, Rare 15, Very Rare 17, Legendary 19

Application by type:

  • Weapon: bonusToHit = bonus, avgDamageBonus = avgDamage
  • Armor: bonusAC = bonus
  • Wand: bonusToHit = bonus, avgDamageBonus = avgDamage, bonusSaveDC = saveDC
  • Wondrous: no automatic combat bonus (freeform design)

sections.heading: Item blueprint
sections.html:
The tool returns a structured blueprint object you can export or copy:

  • name: provided or autogenerated from type and rarity
  • type: one of the supported types
  • attunement: boolean value (true/false)
  • rarity: derived from level
  • levelTuned: clamped level (1–20)
  • targetTags: your optional list
  • ingredients: list of name/quantity/unit
  • craftingCost: numeric gold piece cost if provided
  • craftingTime + craftingTimeUnit: hours/days/weeks as provided
  • craftingRequirement: optional place or specialist requirement
  • lore: optional 100-word description
  • bonusToHit, bonusAC, bonusSaveDC, avgDamageBonus: as applicable
  • notes: summary text if targets were provided

artifactForgeDocs.note: These are baseline heuristics for quick prep on mobile. Adjust or extend to fit your table's tone.

myMonstersDocs.title: My Bestiary – Field Reference
myMonstersDocs.description: Explains every field in the My Bestiary form and how homebrew monsters integrate with the other CRealizr tools.

sections.heading: Identity
sections.html:
• Name — the monster's display name. Must be unique within your library (case-insensitive).
  • Size — one of Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, Huge, or Gargantuan. Matches the 5e size categories.
  • Type — a free-text creature type (e.g. "monstrosity", "undead"). Informational only; not used for filtering.
  • Alignment — a free-text alignment string (e.g. "chaotic evil"). Informational only.

sections.heading: Edition, CR & XP
sections.html:
• Edition — 2014 or 2024. Determines which XP and threshold tables apply when the Encounter Builder uses this monster.
  • Challenge Rating (CR) — ranges from 0 to 30 (including 1/8, 1/4, 1/2). The Encounter Builder uses CR to compute XP budgets and suggest encounter compositions.
  • XP — experience points awarded for defeating this monster. If set to 0, the Encounter Builder falls back to the standard XP-by-CR table.

sections.heading: Stat Block
sections.html:
The stat block section is optional. Filling in any defense or ability score field enables the full stat block on save.

  • AC — Armor Class (0–30).
  • HP — Hit Points.
  • Speed — free-text (e.g. "30 ft, fly 60 ft").
  • Ability Scores — STR, DEX, CON, INT, WIS, CHA (0–30 each). The modifier is calculated automatically as floor((score − 10) / 2).

sections.heading: Damage Per Round (DPR)
sections.html:
DPR fields help the Monster Scaler estimate how dangerous a creature is at different CRs.

  • DPR Min / Max — the low and high ends of expected damage output per round.
  • DPR Range — a human-readable dice expression (e.g. 2d8+4).

sections.heading: Actions
sections.html:
Add as many named actions as needed. Each action has:

  • Action Name — e.g. "Multiattack", "Bite".
  • Damage — optional dice expression (e.g. 2d6+3).

sections.heading: Encounter Data
sections.html:
These fields control how your monster appears in the Encounter Builder's filtered monster pool.

  • Terrain — one or more of dungeon, wilderness, urban, underwater, planar, or any. Monsters tagged any always appear. You can select multiple terrains.
  • Affiliation — the creature's broad category: humanoid, beast, undead, construct, dragon, fiend, celestial, fey, monstrosity, giant, elemental, aberration, plant, or any. Used to filter suggestions by creature category.
  • Genus — an optional grouping tag (e.g. "goblinoid", "dragon", "owlbear"). The autocomplete dropdown shows all genera already used across SRD and homebrew monsters — type a new one or pick an existing one. Used by the Encounter Builder to group thematically related creatures together.

sections.heading: Storage & Portability
sections.html:
• Monsters are stored in your browser's IndexedDB. Clearing browser data removes them.
  • Use Export to download your entire library as a JSON file. This is your backup.
  • Use Import to restore from a previously exported JSON file. Duplicate names are skipped.
  • Exported files can be shared with other DMs or transferred between devices.

sections.heading: Cross-Tool Integration
sections.html:
• Encounter Builder — homebrew monsters appear in the filtered monster pool alongside SRD creatures, matched by CR, terrain, affiliation, and genus.
  • Monster Scaler — homebrew monsters with a stat block can be loaded and scaled to different CRs.

myMonstersDocs.note: All fields follow D&D 5e conventions. Use this page as a reference when building your homebrew library.
